source.authors: C. Caccamo, D. Costa, G. Pellicane
source.title: A comprehensive study of the phase diagram of symmetrical hard-core Yukawa mixtures
source.pdf: pdf/sources_paywall/VLE_LLE_YK/A comprehensive study of the phase diagram of symmetrical hard-core Yukawa mixtures.pdf
source.tables: TABLE I (journal p. 4502, PDF page 5) and TABLE II (journal p. 4503, PDF page 6)
source.transcribed: 2026-08-19, from 200 dpi renders of PDF pages 5 and 6, not from pdftotext
source.transcription_note: pdftotext on this scan is UNUSABLE for these tables. It renders the minus sign as the digit 2 (so P* = -0.25 comes out as '20.25' and -mu = -2.64 as '2 m 2.64'), renders '=' as '5' (nu = 0.7 becomes 'n 50.7'), and renders the parenthesised last-digit uncertainties '(1)' as '~1!'. Every number below was read off the rendered image.

potential.form: v_ij(r) = +inf for r < sigma;  v_ij(r) = -K_ij * exp[-z*(r-sigma)] / (r/sigma) for r >= sigma   [their Eq. (1), sigma = 1]
potential.symmetry: sigma_1 = sigma_2 = 1 (EQUAL DIAMETERS) and K_11 = K_22; the two species differ ONLY in the cross strength.
potential.nu: nu = K_12 / K_11, the cross-to-like ratio. Studied here at nu = 0.7 and nu = 0.9, both with z = 2.45.
potential.reduced_units: T* = k_B T / K_11, rho* = rho * sigma^3, chi_i = rho_i / rho.
potential.note_on_our_convention: IDENTICAL to this project's N=1 contact normalisation extended to a mixture. With sigma = 1 our tail is K_ij * exp(-z*(r-1))/r, so K_11 = K_22 = 1/T*, K_12 = K_21 = nu/T*, and z is the same for every pair. No unit conversion, no LJ->Yukawa mapping. Identical model to Mkanya et al. 2017 (their alpha == this nu, their epsilon_ij == this K_ij); see reference_mkanya2017.json.

warnings: THE LIQUID-VAPOUR BRANCH CARRIES NO COMPOSITION INFORMATION. In Table I, chi_v = chi_l = 0.50 (1) in EVERY row of both mixtures -- forced by the sigma_1 = sigma_2, K_11 = K_22 symmetry. A T-x-y diagram of this VLE is therefore a vertical line at x = 0.5 and measures nothing. Composition only becomes a live variable on the liquid-liquid branch, Table II.

AT nu = 0.7 THE TABLE I LIQUID BRANCH IS METASTABLE, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO. Journal p. 4502: 'the GEMC yielding liquid-vapor coexistence is not able to capture a three phase equilibrium, since this would require, in principle, a third simulation box; it follows that the (homogeneous) liquid branch of the GEMC binodal has to be considered as a metastable one.' Above the crossover density rho*_e = 0.57 the true equilibrium is liquid-liquid. Scoring a theory's STABLE binodal against the nu = 0.7 liquid branch compares against a metastable reference and will read as a model failure. The nu = 0.9 mixture is not flagged this way.

DEMIXING NEEDS det M = 0, NOT dP/drho. The liquid-liquid instability of a symmetric mixture is a COMPOSITION instability: it occurs at fixed total density with the mechanical stability condition still satisfied. Locating it from dbetaP/drho|_{T,x} returns 'no transition'. Use det M = 0 with M_ij = delta_ij/rho_i - chat_ij(0).

SUSPECTED PRINT ERROR, Table II, last row. At rho* = 1.00 the -e column runs 5.19, 5.07, 4.97, 4.91, 4.89, 4.84, then 3.59 (6) at T* = 1.32. Every other isochore is smooth and monotone; 3.59 breaks the trend by ~1.25 where neighbouring steps are ~0.05. It reproduces identically in the render and in pdftotext, so it is printed, not an extraction artefact. Flagged, transcribed verbatim, and excluded from any fit of e(T) along that isochore.

Table II is a set of ISOCHORES, not isobars. Each block fixes rho* and scans T*, so the natural plot is T* vs chi at constant density -- not the constant-pressure T-x-y of chemical engineering. P* is reported (and is negative at the low-T end of rho* = 0.60 and 0.70), it is not controlled.

vle.description: TABLE I. GEMC, N = 400 total particles, two boxes, equimolar. Liquid-vapour coexistence.
vle.sign_note: The paper prints the columns -mu and -e. The values stored here are mu and e THEMSELVES, i.e. already negated back to physical (negative) values. P* is in K_aa/sigma^3 units, mu and e in K_aa units.
vle.uncertainty_note: 'uncert' rows are absolute, converted from the paper's parenthesised last-digit convention (e.g. 0.77 (2) -> 0.02, 0.017 (1) -> 0.001, 3.55 (11) -> 0.11).

lle.description: TABLE II. SGCMC, consolute-type (liquid-liquid) equilibrium, nu = 0.7 only. Each block fixes rho* and scans T*. chi_1 and chi_2 = 1 - chi_1 are the compositions of the two coexisting liquids. THIS is the composition-resolved data set; the VLE table is not.
lle.sign_note: As in the VLE block: the paper prints -e; stored values are e itself. P* is printed signed and stored as printed (negative entries are real).

critical_points.note: GEMC liquid-vapour critical points, obtained by fitting rho_l - rho_v ~ |T - T_cr|^beta (their Eq. 7) with the NONCLASSICAL beta = 0.32 held fixed, plus the law of rectilinear diameters for rho_cr. Journal p. 4502.

mhnc_lv.note: beta was FITTED here (0.34), not held at 0.32 as for the GEMC points. MHNC did not converge for 0.80 < T* < 0.88, so the fit uses binodal points up to T* = 0.8 only.

critical_points.mhnc_lv_nu_0.7: NOT AVAILABLE. 'a calculation of the critical parameters turns out to be not feasible at nu = 0.7, since the solution algorithm of the MHNC ceases to work well before the critical region can be approached.'

cep.note: Critical end point / crossover from liquid-vapour to liquid-liquid equilibrium, nu = 0.7. Obtained by extrapolating the SGCMC line of consolute critical points (fitted with Delta chi ~ |T - T_cr|^beta, beta = 0.32 fixed) to its intersection with the binodal. Journal p. 4504.
cep.qualifier: The paper writes rho*_e ~= 0.57 and T*_e ~= 0.7 (approximate signs in the original); it calls the extrapolation 'very short'. Two significant figures at best.
cep.consolute_composition_note: chi_cr = 0.5 exactly, forced by symmetry, for every consolute critical point. Only T_cr and rho are free.

prior_msa.citation: C. Caccamo and G. Giunta, Mol. Phys. 78, 83 (1993)  [their ref. 15]
prior_msa.why_it_matters: This is the closest precedent to an FMSA-DP calculation on this system: a plain-MSA treatment of the SAME symmetric HCY mixture, giving the liquid-vapour spinodal and the line of consolute critical points at nu = 0.7. Caccamo et al. 1998 assess it on p. 4504: 'although the MSA results are quantitatively discrepant from the simulation and from MHNC predictions (as expected given the thermodynamic inconsistency of the MSA), the location of the liquid-vapor critical density and of the crossover density are fairly well predicted.'
prior_msa.consequence: Sets the bar honestly: on this system MSA is expected to be quantitatively off but topologically right. A first-order FMSA-DP that reproduces rho_cep ~ 0.57 while missing T_cep is the EXPECTED outcome, not a failure.
